```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, comment = NA)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

bayesplot::bayesplot_theme_set(ggplot2::theme_gray())
bayesplot::color_scheme_set(scheme = "brightblue")
```

In this vignette, we use the template model "augm-infection-time" where surveys are conditioned on single introduction.
We load the parameter definitions directly from the model template.

```{r}
# load augmented infection time template
hhsimul <- housepi::HouseholdModel$new("augm-infection-time")

# use example parameters associated to the template model
hhsimul$load_param_template()

# inspect parameter definitions used for simulations
hhsimul$param_defs
```

## Infectivity Profile

To model transmission, 
In `housepi` we follow the convention for infectivity profiles to be function of the generation time.
Generation time is defined as the time from infection to transmission.

Certain profiles will then depend on individual incubation periods $\tau$ as follows:

| Delay | Infector Condition | Infectee Condition | Supported |
|--------------------|------------------|------------------|------------------|
| generation time | \- | \- | &check; |
| from onset to transmission | $\tau_{\rm infector}$ | \- | &check; |
| serial time | $\tau_{\rm infector}$ | $\tau_{\rm infectee}$ | &cross; |

We can provide a custom infectivity profile with the method `$add_infec_profile()` as follows:

```{r}
# we associate a gamma for infectivity profile
hhsimul$add_infec_profile(name = "gamma", args = c(shape = 2.2, scale = 1.3))
```

Bear in mind that each model requiring an infectivity profile has a default profile.

## Simulate an Outbreak

We propose the following definitions for the augmented variable.

```{r}
# associate defininitions from a list
hhsimul$load_augm_list(
  
  # define 'infec_time' as the difference between onset and incubation
  infec_time = "onset_time - incub_period",
  
  # define an 'onset_time' for each individual
  onset_time = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "lnorm",
    args = c(meanlog = 4, sdlog = 0.5),
    max = 365
  ),
  # define an 'incub_period' for each individual
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "gamma",
    # assign arguments of incubation period from parameter definitions
    args = c(shape = "inc_shape@P",  scale = "inc_scale@P"),
    max = 14
  )
)

# append incubation period distribution parameters as constants
hhsimul$load_param_list(inc_shape = 2, inc_scale = 1.1, append = TRUE)
```

We then run a simulation with the method `simulate`.

```{r}
# simulate using the data structure from the survey
dataset <- housepi::survey
dataset$status <- NA
simulated <- hhsimul$simulate(dataset, seed = 3413)

# in addition to final status, we associated  augmented variables
# incubation period onset time
head(simulated)

# assume onsets after 6 PM are reported to next day
is_infec <- simulated$status == 1
simulated$onset_date <- NA
simulated[is_infec, "onset_date"] <- sapply(
  simulated[is_infec, "onset_time"],
  # simulation onset date > 18/24
  function(x) floor(ifelse((x %% 1) > 0.75, x + 1, x))
)

# remove onobserved quantities simulated dataset
simulated$incub_period <- NULL
simulated$onset_time <- NULL
simulated$infec_time <- NULL

head(simulated)
```

## Validate the Simulation

We can check that inference returns the parameters used for the simulation.

```{r}
# make a deep clone of simulation object to re-use previous definitions
hhmodel <- hhsimul$clone(deep = TRUE)

# load definitions from list (automatically drop previous definitions)
hhmodel$load_augm_list(
  infec_time = "onset_time - incub_period",
  onset_time = list(
    value = "onset_date@D",
    rule = "norm", scale = 0.25, from = "onset_date@D"
  ),
  incub_period = list(
    init_rand = TRUE,
    model = "gamma", args = c(shape = "inc_shape@P", scale = "inc_scale@P"),
    max = 14, rule = "draw"
  )
)

# perform the inference
# note: NA onset dates of healthy individuals will raise a warning
hhmodel$infer(simulated, n_chains = 3, n_steps = 10000,
              n_adapt = 2000, n_burnin = 1000, thin = 10,
              seed = 3731, progress = 20)
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=4, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# use bayesplot to plot the posterior draws
library(bayesplot)
mcmc_trace(hhmodel$traces)
```

```{r, fig.width=5, fig.height=2.5, fig.fullwidth=TRUE, out.height="auto", fig.align="center"}
# compute Rhat values associate to inferred parameters
mask <- hhmodel$param_defs$name[!hhmodel$param_defs$const]
rhat_values <- sapply(hhmodel$traces, posterior::rhat)[mask]

# use bayesplot to showcase Rhat statistics
mcmc_rhat(rhat_values) + yaxis_text(hjust = 1)
```

Here we performed R-hat diagnostics computing the values of $\hat{R}$ with [rstan](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rstan/).

Finally we wrap all together to compare to parameters used for simulation.

```{r}
# collect the results
traces <- hhmodel$traces
traces$loglikelihood <- NULL
estimates <- posterior::summarise_draws(traces)

# compare results to parameter values used for simulation
simul_param_defs <- hhsimul$param_defs
imask <- simul_param_defs$const == FALSE
inames <- simul_param_defs[imask, ]$name
```

```{r, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,}
library(dplyr)
library(flextable)
cbind(simulated = simul_param_defs[imask, ]$value, estimates) |>
  tibble::rownames_to_column("parameter") |>
  mutate(inferred = sprintf("%0.4f [%0.4f, %0.4f]", mean, q5, q95)) |>
  select(variable, simulated, inferred) |>
  flextable() |>
  separate_header() |>
  theme_vanilla() |>
  bold(j = ~ variable, bold = TRUE) |>
  autofit()
```
